transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm doing this right... um, I came in because I've been having a little bit of trouble lately. It's probably just stress from my job—I do personal care, so I'm always on my feet, you know? 

But... well, I've been hearing things. I feel a little silly even saying it out loud, and I'm sorry to bother you with it, but I keep hearing these voices. They're as clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio, saying my name and... and telling me my work is being judged. Even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody else is there. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, doesn't it? Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be telling you?
Do the voices ever tell you to do something or give you instructions?

Oh, no, no, they don't do that. I mean, they don't give me orders or tell me to do anything bad or... or anything like that. I wouldn't listen to them if they did, I promise. 

They mostly just talk about me, or say my name, like I mentioned. It's really just a nuisance more than anything else. I'm sorry if I made it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe around... nine months? Give or take? 

I really tried to ignore them for a long time, you know, because I didn't want to make a fuss. And the worries I have about my work being watched—that's been going on for about the same amount of time. Nine months or so. I kept hoping it would just go away on its own if I didn't pay it any mind. 

I'm sorry I waited so long to come in, I really am. I just didn't want to be a bother. Is nine months a really long time to wait? I hope I haven't messed anything up by not coming sooner...
Do you believe that your work is actually being judged or watched by others?

Well, um... I know it probably sounds a little silly, and I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything... but yes, I do. Or, I did. 

I just... I got it in my head that the other home-care agency in town, and maybe some people from the local library, were watching me. I thought they were looking at my little paintings I do at home, and going through my client papers. I thought they were trying to steal a special chance or an opportunity that was meant for me. 

I know it sounds far-fetched. People told me it didn't make any sense, and I tried so hard to listen to them, I really did. I didn't want to cause any trouble. But deep down, I just... I still knew they were doing it. It felt so real to me. 

I'm sorry, that's probably not what you wanted to hear, is it? I hope I'm not making things too difficult for you by saying all this...
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or have trouble keeping your thoughts organized in your head?

Well, um... I guess sometimes my mind does get a little busy. I really try to keep everything neat and tidy up there, but... sometimes my thoughts just run so fast. 

Like, one minute I'll be thinking about making sure my client takes their medicine, and then right away I'm worrying about the rent, and then I'm trying to think of a title for one of my paintings, and then I'm focused on some message I heard in a song on the radio. It all just piles up so quickly, and I can't seem to slow it down enough to make sense of it all. 

I try really hard to keep it together, though, I promise. I don't let it affect my work if I can help it. I'm sorry if that sounds disorganized... I hope I'm explaining it okay. Does that make sense?
Do you have difficulty completing tasks or achieving your goals due to your thoughts or behaviors?

Well, um... I really do try my best to get everything done. I want my clients to be well taken care of, and I take my job very seriously, I promise. But... I suppose there have been a few little moments where I get a bit... sidetracked? 

I feel so bad admitting this, because I don't want you to think I'm not a good worker. But sometimes, when I'm at a client's house, I just... I stop what I'm supposed to be doing. I'll take out the medical gloves, and the little plastic pill cups, and maybe some scraps of yarn from my crocheting, and I'll just... start lining them all up. In these specific patterns. Or sometimes I'll just stand out in the hallway, perfectly still, just staring and waiting. Like I'm supposed to receive some sort of signal before I can move again. 

I always snap out of it and finish my chores, though! I really do. I just... I get caught up in those little moments sometimes. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds very strange and unprofessional. Does that mean I'm doing a bad job? I really hope it doesn't...
Do you find yourself repeating certain behaviors or actions over and over, even when you don't need to?

Well, um... not exactly? I mean, I really try to just do things once and move on, like a normal person. I don't want to waste time or anything. 

I guess I did mention lining up the pill cups and the gloves earlier... but I don't really do that over and over again all day. It's just... every now and then, I might get a little particular about how things are arranged. But I don't think it's anything too unusual. I just like things to be orderly, you know? 

I really try not to let any little habits get in the way of my work or my life. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you still believe that your work is being watched or judged by others, or have your thoughts about that changed over time?

Well, um... I guess I do still have some of those thoughts. I really try not to let them bother me, and I know it probably sounds a little silly to say out loud... I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. 

But... for a while now, I just got it in my head that the people from the other home-care agency in town, and even some folks from the local library, were... watching me. Like they were keeping an eye on my paintings and my client papers. I just had this feeling that they were trying to steal some special chance or opportunity that was meant for me. 

My friends and family told me it made no sense, and I really tried to listen to them, I promise! I didn't want to make a fuss. But... deep down, I just knew they were doing it. Even when people said it was impossible, I couldn't shake the feeling. I still struggle with it sometimes. 

I'm sorry if that sounds crazy. I know it's not a very normal way to think. I really hope you don't think less of me for feeling that way... I am trying my best to be reasonable about it. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself jumping from one topic to another when talking to someone?

Well, um... I really try to stay focused when I'm talking to people. I want to be a good listener, and I know it's polite to stick to the subject. I don't want anyone to think I'm scatterbrained or rude, I promise. 

But... I guess sometimes it's just really hard to keep my words in a straight line. It's not that I'm trying to confuse anyone! It's just... my mind gets going so fast. It's like my thoughts are running a race, and I can't keep up with them. 

One second I'll be thinking about whether I gave my client their medicine, and then before I can even finish that thought, I'm worrying about how I'm going to pay my rent, and then suddenly I'm trying to come up with a title for one of my paintings, and then I'm thinking about a message I heard in a song on the radio... and it all just spills out of my mouth before I can slow it down enough to make sense. 

I try so hard to catch myself and apologize when I do it. I know it must be frustrating to listen to. I really hope I'm not doing it too much right now... am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you often have trouble finding the right words when trying to express your thoughts?

Well, um... I don't think so? I mean, I really try to communicate clearly. I know how important it is to make sure people understand what I'm trying to say, especially with my clients. I want to be as helpful as possible. 

I guess sometimes, if I'm feeling a little overwhelmed or if my thoughts are going a bit too fast like I mentioned before, I might pause for a second to find the right word. But I don't think it's anything too bad. I always manage to get my point across eventually. 

I try to read and keep my vocabulary up so I don't sound foolish. I hope I've been expressing myself okay today? I really want to make sure I'm giving you clear answers and not being confusing.
Have your thoughts about being watched or judged by others ever completely gone away for a while, or have they always been present to some degree?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound too difficult or, you know, stubborn. I know I'm supposed to be getting better, and I want you to know I really am trying my hardest to let those thoughts go. 

But... to be completely honest, they didn't just go away when the other things calmed down. There was this time... after my energy finally dropped back to normal and I was actually sleeping through the night again... I thought everything would be completely fine. I really did! But the belief that those people were tracking my work and judging me... it just kept going. And the voices, too. They stuck around for several weeks after I started resting better. 

I know it probably sounds like I wasn't trying hard enough to ignore them, but I promise I was. I just couldn't make them stop right away. I'm sorry if that's disappointing to hear... I know it's not the right way to think. Does that make sense, though? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to others when you're speaking?

Well, um... I really hope not. I try my very best to make sure people understand me, I promise. Even when my mind is going a little too fast, like I mentioned earlier, I... I always try to tie it all together so it still makes sense. I don't want anyone to think I'm just talking nonsense, especially not my clients. They really rely on me to be clear. 

I don't think my thoughts are disjointed... at least, nobody has ever complained to me that they don't understand what I'm saying. I mean, I'm making sense to you right now, aren't I? I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers. I'd feel just awful if I was sitting here confusing you.
Do you often feel like you have trouble staying on topic when you're talking to someone?

Oh, goodness, no, I don't think I do. I really try to be mindful of that. I know how frustrating it can be when someone just rambles and wastes your time, and I would just hate to be a bother to anyone like that. Especially at work, I always make sure to focus on whatever my clients need to talk about. 

I guess... well, maybe if I'm having one of those days where I've got a lot of extra energy, I might get a little carried away and drift for just a second, but I always pull it right back to the main point. I really do try to stay focused. I've been doing okay staying on track with you today, right? I'm trying so hard to just answer your questions directly so I don't take up too much of your time.
Have there been any times when you didn't believe people were watching or judging you at all?

Well, um... I really wish I could say yes, because I know it sounds so silly when I say it out loud. I want to be the kind of person who just brushes things off, I really do. But... no, I haven't really had a time where I didn't believe it. 

I know I shouldn't think this way, and I'm so sorry if it sounds like I'm just being paranoid... but I just got it in my head that the other home-care agency in town, and even some folks from the library, were watching my paintings and going through my client papers. I just... I felt so sure they were trying to steal some kind of opportunity that was meant for me. 

My friends and family told me it made absolutely no sense, and I tried so hard to agree with them because I didn't want to upset anybody or seem crazy. But even when they said that, deep down, I just knew they were doing it. I couldn't shake it. I'm sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear, and I really am trying to be better about it. Am I making things too difficult by holding onto that? I just want to be completely honest with you.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't have any thoughts about being watched or judged at all?

Well, um... I really wish I could say yes to that, too. I know it's probably exhausting for you to hear, and I'm so sorry if I'm being a difficult patient. I really want to be doing better, I promise. But... no, I haven't really had a break from it. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, and I hope you won't judge me too harshly for this... the fixed fears about people watching my work, and... and the voices I mentioned earlier... they've been happening pretty steadily for about nine months now. 

I try so hard to just ignore it all and focus on my clients, because I don't want anyone to think I'm doing a bad job. I just want to be helpful and do things right. Nine months probably sounds like such a long time to let this go on, doesn't it? I should have tried harder to snap out of it sooner... I really hope you don't think less of me for that. I am trying my best, I really am.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other?

Oh, um, disconnected? No, I don't think so. I really try to keep my thoughts organized, especially for my clients. I know it's so important to be clear and focused when you're helping people, and I'd just hate to seem scattered or confused around them. 

Sometimes, if I'm feeling a little tired or overwhelmed, maybe my mind wanders just a tiny bit, but I always catch myself. I really make an effort to keep everything tied together so I can be as helpful as possible. My thoughts usually flow pretty well, I think. I haven't been jumping around too much while we've been talking, have I? I really hope I'm making sense for you.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't have any thoughts about people watching or judging you at all?

Well, um... I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself or not explaining it right. I really don't want to waste your time. But... no, I haven't really had a time where those thoughts just went away. 

Like I was saying before... I just couldn't shake the feeling that the other home-care agency, and those people from the library, were looking at my paintings and my client papers. I know it sounds so foolish when I say it again... but I just felt so certain they were trying to steal some special chance that was supposed to be mine. 

I know my family said it didn't make any sense, and I really, really tried to just agree with them and be agreeable. I hate causing a fuss. But even then... I just knew they were doing it. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't think that way. Am I making things too complicated by bringing this up again? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question exactly the way you need me to.
Have you ever had a period, no matter how short, where you didn't believe people were watching or judging you?

Oh, um... I feel terrible because you're asking again, and I must not be explaining myself very well at all. I'm so sorry. I know I'm probably being difficult, and I really don't mean to be. 

But... no, I really haven't had a break from it. I wish I could tell you that I did, because I know that's probably what you want to hear, and I'd love to say I've been doing better. But those feelings... they just haven't stopped. I try so hard to push them away and just focus on being a good aide for my clients, but the thoughts are always just... there. 

I'm sorry, I know that's the same answer I gave before. I really hope you're not frustrated with me. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often find yourself saying things that don't make sense to others?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I really try to be very careful with how I speak, especially because of my work. My clients rely on me to be clear and helpful, so I always make sure I'm making sense when I talk to them. I'd feel just awful if I confused them or if they couldn't understand me. 

Sometimes, maybe if I'm just very tired after a long shift, I might stumble over a word or two, but I think everyone does that, right? I always try to correct myself right away. I haven't been saying anything confusing today, have I? I really hope I've been making sense to you. I'm trying my best to answer everything clearly.
Do you often find yourself losing your train of thought while speaking?

Oh, no, I don't think so... at least, I really hope not. I try very hard to stay focused on what I'm saying, especially because I know you're busy and I want to be helpful. 

I mean, I suppose sometimes if there's a lot going on, I might need a tiny second to gather my thoughts, but I don't think I just drift off or forget what I was talking about. I always try to finish my sentences and make sure I get my point across properly. 

I haven't been doing that today, have I? Losing my place, I mean? I'm really trying to pay close attention to your questions so I can give you the best answers.
